formats.key: exec(address safe, address to, uint256 value, bytes data, bytes32 requestId, uint256 deadline, bytes signatures)
effects: The Safe at `safe` calls `to` with `value` wei of the Safe's ETH and `data`, as a plain CALL (operation fixed to 0), through execTransactionFromModuleReturnData.
Whatever the inner call does acts on the Safe's assets, allowances and roles, with the Safe as msg.sender.
The contract marks `requestId` as spent for this Safe, so the same authorization cannot run again.
The call reverts after `deadline`, when the request id is already spent, when the owner signatures do not meet the Safe's threshold, or when the inner call fails.
The transaction signer is only a relayer: no ETH leaves the signer (the function is not payable) and none of the signer's own tokens move, apart from gas.
formats.shown: "Run Safe transaction", with the Safe, an ETH value, the deadline, the raw request id, the target, and the inner call decoded by the target's descriptor, e.g. "Set minter: Bob, true".

findings.title: exec labels the Safe's outgoing ETH only "Value", so the signer may think the ETH comes from their own wallet.
findings.evidence: UnorderedExecutor.exec is non-payable and forwards the value from the Safe: `ISafe(safe).execTransactionFromModuleReturnData(to, value, data, 0)`. The descriptor field is `{"path": "value", "label": "Value", "format": "amount"}`. Case 0 shows "Value: 0 ETH" right under "From safe", and nothing says who pays it.
findings.fix: Change the label to "ETH sent by Safe" so it is clear the Safe pays and not the relaying signer.

findings.title: The exec intent "Run Safe transaction" is generic, so only the nested Action field names the real effect.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: `"intent": "Run Safe transaction"`. The real effect comes from the arbitrary `(to, value, data)` that exec forwards. In case 0 the inner action "Set minter" appears only inside the Action field.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent that names the Safe and the target, e.g. "Run Safe transaction from {safe} on {to}". The nested intent cannot go into the outer sentence.

findings.title: exec shows the request id as a raw 32-byte hex value that changes nothing about who gets what.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: `{"path": "requestId", "label": "Request id", "format": "raw"}`. In exec, `used[safe][requestId] = true` only stops a replay. Case 0 shows "0x0a0a…0a".
findings.fix: Leave it out, or keep it as optional bookkeeping for reviewers who match it against the off-chain proposal.
